papers.title: Frames and representing systems in Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: We study representing systems of Cauchy kernels or dilations of a given function in Hardy spaces. We give a complete geometric description of countable sets $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{D}$ such that the system $\{\hat{k}_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of normalized Cauchy kernels forms a generalized frame in the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{D})$ with $p \in (1, \infty)$ with respect to a particular coefficient space. For a wide class of functions we construct representing systems of their dilations in $H^2$. We also obtain a linear method for expanding functions in series of Cauchy kernels in $H^2$.

papers.title: On Koebe theorem for Sobolev mappings on Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider mappings between domains of two Riemannian surfaces. The main subject of the investigation are families of homeomorphisms with moduli inequalities. For such families, we obtain the uniform openness (uniform lightness). As a consequence, we obtain similar results for homeomorphisms of Sobolev classes with finite distortion whenever its maximal dilatations have a majorant integrable on almost all concentric circles. In particular, we obtain the Koebe-type theorem for both direct and inverse Sobolev mappings.

papers.title: On the uniform algebras generated by powers of the coordinates and smooth functions on compact subsets of $\Bbb C^N$
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\Bbb C^N$ be compact and let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_N)$ be a smooth map on a neighbourhood of $K$. We give sufficient conditions for the algebra generated by $z_1^{m_1},\dots,z_N^{m_N}$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$ (or by all monomials of degree $n$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$) to be dense in $C(K)$. We appropriately extend the techniques developed in our previous works [3,4,6] and [8] for algebras of functions on the complex plane to tackle the problem in the several-variable setting. More precisely, the argument separates a purely algebraic reduction, in which the rotated graphs are glued one coordinate at a time, from the study of the single graph of $f$. For the latter we give an exact computation of the Levi form of $|w-f|^{2p}$, which yields a Hermitian matrix criterion on the polynomial hull of the graph; a criterion by peak functions that removes the invertibility hypothesis from a theorem of Preskenis; a division theorem for $f_j=\bar k_jh_j$ with degenerate holomorphic factors $h_j$; and a treatment of the singular set $\{\det(\partial f_i/\partial\bar z_j)=0\}$, which in several variables is not finite. The angle $\pi/m_j$ in the reduction is shown to be sharp.

papers.title: Lempert and pluricomplex Green functions near non-semipositive boundary points
papers.abstract: We study the two-step Lempert function and the pluricomplex Green function near a non-semipositive boundary point of a bounded domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove a sharp upper estimate for the two-step Lempert function in terms of the local boundary scale $H_D$, and obtain matching estimates for the pluricomplex Green function. As a consequence, these quantities have the same boundary behaviour as the Kobayashi distance. For the usual Lempert function, we prove an upper estimate of order $\sqrt{H_D}$, which implies the optimal local $1/4$-H\"older estimate, and determine its precise boundary behaviour along the real normal.

papers.title: Quasihyperbolic geodesics in the twice-puntured plane
papers.abstract: We study quasihyperbolic distance and geodesic uniqueness in the plane punctured at 0 and 2. For endpoints on the perpendicular bisector of the punctures and on opposite sides of the real axis, the distance is the smaller of the length of the vertical segment and the least length of a feasible detour. For symmetric endpoints 1 \pm it with t > 0, the geodesic is unique precisely when arsinh t + arctan t < \pi. At equality there are exactly three geodesic images, and above the threshold there are exactly two. For arbitrary endpoints, we derive variational formulas for the distance in terms of admissible logarithmic spirals and their contacts with the bisector. The minimizing candidates in these formulas give all geodesic images and yield a length-comparison criterion for uniqueness.

papers.title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Generalized Hartogs Triangles
papers.abstract: We study zeros of the Bergman kernel on the generalized Hartogs triangles $H_\gamma=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^\gamma<|z_2|<1\}$. For every real $1<\gamma<2$, suitable sections near the singular vertex contain exactly $\lceil(\gamma-1)^{-1}\rceil-1$ zeros in a prescribed disk, all of them simple. This answers a question of Edholm and Mathew [\emph{Math. Z.} \textbf{313} (2026)] and, together with the known cases, shows that $H_\gamma$ has a zero-free Bergman kernel precisely when $\gamma$ is the reciprocal of a positive integer. We also fix the second kernel argument and a complex line in the first argument, and prove that the total number of zeros on the admissible section is comparable to $(\gamma-1)^{-1}$ as $\gamma\to1^+$; a comparable number are simple and nonreal. For the sections near the vertex, all but at most one of the counted zeros concentrate near the unit circle, and the angular counting error is uniformly bounded.

papers.title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
papers.abstract: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link. On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities. The proof uses a compact composition operator to control the spectrum on the Zariski tangent space and obtains a positive grading from the resulting spectral condition.

papers.title: Estimates of the Schwarz constant for monogenic functions in $\mathbb R^3$
papers.abstract: The Schwarz lemma bounds the differential at the origin of a holomorphic self-map of the unit disc fixing $0$: $|f'(0)|\le1$. For monogenic maps in $\mathbb R^3$, the optimal constant is not known. Let $\mathcal M$ be the class of monogenic functions $f$ from the unit ball of $\mathbb R^3$ to the reduced quaternions with $|f|\le1$ and $f(0)=0$, and let $C_*=\sup_{\mathcal M}|f'(0)|$, where $f'=\partial_0f$ is the hypercomplex derivative. We show that $\frac{80}{61}\le C_*\le1.35784$. Thus the classical bound $1$ fails, while $C_*$ stays below the sharp constant $\frac32$ for harmonic maps of the ball into itself. The estimates rest on a reduction, by rotation covariance and averaging about the $x_0$-axis, to a convex extremal problem in one variable for zonal harmonic functions. Lower bounds come from restricting this problem to polynomials, and upper bounds from its dual formulation in terms of vector fields on the sphere.

papers.title: Families of (Pluri)subharmonic Functions and Separate Subharmonicity
papers.abstract: We study the singular sets of pointwise bounded-above envelopes of families of functions. For families of subharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C$, of plurisubharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^N$, and, more generally, of functions subharmonic in each complex variable separately, we prove that the singular set of a pointwise bounded-above envelope is relatively closed and nowhere dense. In contrast, for $N\ge3$ we construct a sequence of subharmonic functions on $\mathbb R^N$ whose upper envelope is finite everywhere but nowhere locally bounded above. We also characterize the singular sets that arise for admissible classes of functions, both with and without a continuity assumption, and give applications to separately subharmonic functions.

papers.title: Removability Criteria for Separately Harmonic and Subharmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Cegrell and Sadullaev showed that a separately harmonic and subharmonic function is subharmonic outside the product of two closed nowhere dense sets. We obtain sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the second set, under which the function is subharmonic on the whole domain. In particular, we prove that this holds whenever the second set is polar.

papers.title: Renormalized volume, Generalized Loewner energy, and Grunsky determinant of multiply connected domains
papers.abstract: We define and study three M\"obius invariant functionals for multiply connected planar domains with finitely many boundary components: the Loewner energy, the renormalized volume, and the Grunsky determinant. Using quasiconformal variations, we prove that when the boundary curves are sufficiently regular, the three functionals differ only by a modulus-dependent constant. We also prove that the Loewner energy is finite if and only if every boundary curve is a Weil--Petersson quasicircle. Moreover, we prove that the three functionals all attain their unique extremal value at the circle domains. In particular, the Loewner energy is zero if and only if it is evaluated at a circle domain. Finally, we use the minimization of Loewner energy to give a new proof of the finitely connected version of Koebe uniformization theorem.

papers.title: The q-Jack Lemma and Its Applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a Jackson $q$-difference analogue of Jack's lemma and its higher-order extension by Miller and Mocanu, which serve as cornerstone tools in geometric function theory and differential subordination. Applying this foundation, we establish $q$-counterparts of Nunokawa's boundary theorem and the Miller-Mocanu subordination lemma, and deduce applications to circular enclosure bounds. All obtained results naturally recover their classical counterparts in the limiting case as $q \to 1^-$.

papers.title: Normal Squeezing and Strict Pseudoconvexity
papers.abstract: We prove that a boundary point $p$ of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is locally $C^{2,\alpha}$ near $p$, $0<\alpha\le1$, and the squeezing function tends to one along the inward normal. Neither finite type nor convexity is assumed. Under local $C^2$ regularity alone, the same limit gives the normal logarithmic Bergman-kernel growth exponent $n+1$. The proof uses normalized Bergman-kernel profiles and holomorphic translation semigroups on the ball.

papers.title: Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
papers.abstract: For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $\Omega$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partial\Omega$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $\Omega = U$.

papers.title: Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk. As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.

papers.title: Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire solution of order less than 1 of the linear difference equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=0}^{m}P_j(z)\Delta^j f(z)=0, \qquad P_m\not\equiv0, \end{equation*} where $P_0,\ldots,P_m$ are polynomials. Applying the inverse Newton transform $\Scal$, which sends $\fall{z}{n}$ to $z^n$, we obtain a function $g=\Scal f$ satisfying a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. We then show that the completely regular growth of $g$ transfers to $f$. Consequently, $f$ is of completely regular growth and the zeros of \(f\) are regularly distributed. An example involving the \(\Gamma\) function is given to shows that the condition order less than $ 1$ cannot be relaxed.

papers.title: Equilibrium points of logarithmic potentials
papers.abstract: We construct logarithmic potentials with positive masses at a sequence of points tending to infinity and with no critical points. These potentials can have any prescribed order $\rho \in [1/2, 1)$; for $\rho = 1/2$ we obtain examples of both normal and maximal type. For $1/2 < \rho < 1$, the masses at conjugate poles are prescribed by a power law. We determine the pole asymptotics and the angular growth of these potentials. For sums of simple fractions with absolutely summable complex residues and nonzero sum of residues, we prove the existence of infinitely many zeros and compare their counting function with that of the poles.

papers.title: Extremal disc packings in compact hyperbolic surfaces of minimal genus
papers.abstract: A compact hyperbolic surface is $k$-extremal if it contains $k$ disjoint embedded discs of the largest possible radius; such surfaces are uniformized by surface subgroups of the triangle groups $\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We determine all extremal $k$-packings in every $k$-extremal surface of minimal genus, orientable of genus $2$ and non-orientable of genus $3$: $373$ surface groups in total, all treated in a unified way; $264$ of them had never been studied before. The computation is automatic and verified in exact arithmetic, each packing being certified by an element $\alpha\in\mathrm{PGL}_2$ over an explicit number field with $\alpha^{-1}K\alpha<\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We also obtain the full isometry groups of these surfaces. In every surface but one, all the extremal packings are related by isometries. The exception is the genus two surface $X_6$ of Girondo and Gonz\'alez-Diez, which has exactly five extremal $4$-packings, one invariant under all isometries and four forming an orbit; it is also the only one of these surfaces uniformized by two non-conjugate subgroups of the same triangle group, and we show that the two facts are equivalent. We find its equation, $y^2=x^6+2\sqrt{3}\,i\,x^3+1$. The results form a catalogue with detailed data and pictures of every surface (packings, isometries, Weierstrass points, Dirichlet domains), distributed with programs that allow the reader to consult it and to reproduce it completely.

papers.title: Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
papers.abstract: Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface. With a cusped hyperbolic metric $h$ prescribed, we investigate the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ of such ideal polyhedral realizations and their possible degeneration. Particularly in the case of tori, we show that the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and that the induced map to Teichm\"uller space of the closed torus is a $C^1$-embedding. This map extends to a bijection from the closure of $\mathcal{P}(h)$ onto the whole Teichm\"uller space, where the added points are degenerate surfaces. This is dual to the Kojima-Mizushima-Tan conjecture about circle patterns on closed surfaces with complex projective structures.

papers.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Koll\'ar. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume. The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Koll\'ar's gluing techniques.

papers.title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via Kähler Reduction
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant K\"ahler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For a unitary partial flag manifold, we realize the given metric by K\"ahler reduction of a Hermitian vector space. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.

papers.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

papers.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
papers.abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

papers.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
papers.abstract: The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by \[ \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}: \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}} \left| \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}} {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2} \right|<1 \right\}, \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0 \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $\mu_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,\mu_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $\Psi_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[ \Psi_{\mathbb H}(\xi_1, \xi_2,\lambda_1,\lambda_2) = \left(\frac{\lambda_1(\xi_1-1)}{2}, \frac{\xi_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \ \frac{\lambda_1\lambda_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \ \xi_1 \xi_2\lambda_1\lambda_2 \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $\Psi_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.
